**Tipo de sesión:** brainstorming
**Referencia anterior:** handoff-2026-08-10-223511-991.md

## Contexto inmediato
Added Apéndice F to truco-rules.md: 36 presencial situations cataloged as F.1 (motor makes impossible), F.2 (motor auto-validates), F.3 (motor auto-sanctions), F.4 (fair play / undetectable), F.5 (motor MUST implement), F.6 (motor MUST NOT implement). Drives a clear scope for engine implementation.

## Trabajo completado
- Cataloged 36 problematic presencial situations across 6 categories (F.1-F.6)
- F.1 — 12 situations that the engine makes impossible (dropping cards, accidental reveals, dealing errors, etc.)
- F.2 — 10 situations the engine auto-validates (minting envido/flor, calling non-canonical cantos, etc.)
- F.3 — 8 situations the engine auto-sanctions (timer, no-show cards, offline, etc.)
- F.4 — 5 situations the engine CANNOT detect (strategic bluffing, collusion, lag)
- F.5 — 8 things the engine MUST implement (validation, auto-detect Flor, timer, etc.)
- F.6 — 10 things the engine MUST NOT implement (irrelevant presencial rules)
- Updated brain79 INDEX.md with Apéndice F reference

## Trabajo pendiente
- Engine implementation: TypeScript state machine under `src/engine/` (or `engine/`)
- Use concept/truco-simulations.md (12 scenarios) as oracle for unit tests
- Apéndice F.5 is the must-implement checklist; F.6 is the can-skip list — these directly inform engine scope
- Consider extracting the envido betting table (§6.3.1) and the "rules that are now moot" (§F.6) into a config-driven approach

## Conocimiento pendiente de promoción (a wiki)
- The presencial truco rulebook contains ~30+ clauses whose sole purpose is handling physical-world edge cases (drops, accidental reveals, dealing errors) — these become dead code in an online engine
- Online auto-validation flips the burden: in presencial, the rival had to verify; online, the engine verifies continuously and applies sanctions instantly
- Strategic bluffing (F.4.1) remains legitimate and is not policed — the engine only polices accidental/lying situations, not strategic deception
- Colusión (F.4.4) and smurfing (F.4.5) are out of scope for the game engine — they belong to the platform's anti-cheat layer

## Gotchas
- F.5 (must-implement) is the engine spec — F.6 (must-not-implement) is the explicit non-goals list; both are derived directly from the presencial rulebook
- F.4 (fair play) means the engine cannot replace social norms entirely — strategic bluffing is fine, but collusion detection is platform-level
- Do NOT start engine implementation until all product decisions (Appendix D) are confirmed by the team

Begin TypeScript engine implementation in `src/engine/`, using §17 state machine outline + Apéndice F.5 scope + truco-simulations.md oracle.
